title: Mixed algebraic simplification and verification

steps.title: Sort the matching tiles
steps.action: Place both x terms in one bin.
steps.narration: Both tiles contain one x, so add their coefficients.

steps.title: Combine coefficients
steps.action: Add three and five, then keep x.
steps.narration: Three x units and five x units make eight x units.

worked_examples.repair: Count the x tiles and keep the x label.

steps.title: Separate kinds
steps.action: Move positive two to the constant bin and minus a beside four a.
steps.narration: A constant cannot join an a term.

steps.title: Read the hidden coefficient
steps.action: Write minus a as minus one a.
steps.narration: The sign belongs to the a term.

steps.title: Collect the a terms
steps.action: Four minus one is three.
steps.narration: Leave the constant two unchanged.

worked_examples.misconception: Combining two with a or losing the minus.
worked_examples.repair: Place different powers and constants in separate bins.

steps.title: Draw both distribution arrows
steps.action: Multiply two by x and by positive three.
steps.narration: The outside factor belongs to every term inside the bracket.

steps.title: Find the matching x terms
steps.action: Group two x and one x; six stays a constant.
steps.narration: Only like terms share a bin.

steps.title: Combine the x count
steps.action: Two x plus one x equals three x.
steps.narration: The final constant is still six.

worked_examples.misconception: Multiplying only the x inside the bracket.
worked_examples.repair: Trace both arrows before collecting terms.

steps.title: Multiply both bracket terms
steps.action: Five times y is five y; five times negative two is negative ten.
steps.narration: The negative constant keeps its sign.

steps.title: Sort matching y terms
steps.action: Five y and negative two y belong together.
steps.narration: Negative ten is not a y term.

steps.title: Combine y counts
steps.action: Five minus two is three.
steps.narration: Three y minus ten is the simplified expression.

worked_examples.misconception: Writing +10 after distributing a negative term.
worked_examples.repair: Attach a minus card to the two before multiplying.

steps.title: Keep the signed multiplier together
steps.action: Negative three times t is negative three t; negative three times negative four is plus twelve.
steps.narration: Two negative factors make a positive constant.

steps.title: Place the remaining t beside negative three t
steps.action: The extra t is positive one t.
steps.narration: Collect only like variable terms.

steps.title: Add signed coefficients
steps.action: Negative three plus one is negative two.
steps.narration: The plus twelve survives unchanged.

worked_examples.misconception: Turning the bracket constant into negative twelve.
worked_examples.repair: Show the two negative chips multiplying before writing plus twelve.

steps.title: Split the complete numerator
steps.action: Divide both twelve x and eight by four.
steps.narration: The division bar covers the two-term numerator.

steps.title: Calculate both quotients
steps.action: Twelve x over four is three x; eight over four is two.
steps.narration: Keep the additional three x outside the quotient.

steps.title: Combine like terms
steps.action: Three x plus three x gives six x.
steps.narration: Two is a constant and remains separate.

worked_examples.misconception: Dividing twelve x but not eight.
worked_examples.repair: Draw one quotient lane for each numerator term.

steps.title: Expand both independent groups
steps.action: First group becomes six a minus four; second becomes three a plus three.
steps.narration: Keep the two arrow pairs visible.

steps.title: Build variable and constant bins
steps.action: Put six a with three a, and negative four with positive three.
steps.narration: Do not combine unlike kinds.

steps.title: Total both bins
steps.action: Nine a and negative one remain.
steps.narration: The simplified result is nine a minus one.

worked_examples.repair: Complete and colour both bracket paths before sorting.

steps.title: Distribute minus one
steps.action: Subtract two x and subtract negative three, which becomes plus three.
steps.narration: The minus belongs to every bracket term.

steps.title: Group the x terms
steps.action: Four x minus two x leaves two x.
steps.narration: Positive three remains outside the group.

steps.title: State the result
steps.action: Write two x plus three.
steps.narration: Check the flipped sign on the former negative three.

worked_examples.misconception: Changing only the first bracket sign.
worked_examples.repair: Mark a negative-one arrow to each term.

steps.title: Divide each numerator term
steps.action: Eighteen p squared divided by six p is three p; twelve p divided by six p is two.
steps.narration: Cancellation needs p to be nonzero.

steps.title: Expose the constant and extra p
steps.action: Keep two as a constant while adding the outside two p.
steps.narration: The divisor restriction remains attached.

steps.title: Collect p terms
steps.action: Three p plus two p is five p.
steps.narration: The original expression is undefined at zero, even though the simplified form is defined there.

worked_examples.misconception: Cancelling p at zero or turning 12p÷6p into 2p.
worked_examples.repair: Cancel one p only after stating p≠0.

steps.title: Separate powers
steps.action: Place x squared terms in one row and x terms in another.
steps.narration: One x and x squared are unlike term types.

steps.title: Read the signs in each row
steps.action: Three minus one square units; two plus four linear units.
steps.narration: Only the coefficients in the same row combine.

steps.title: Complete both rows
steps.action: Two x squared plus six x.
steps.narration: Do not invent an x cubed term.

worked_examples.misconception: Combining x and x² as x³.
worked_examples.repair: Use separate x and x² tiles, never multiply while adding.

worked_examples.q: A learner writes 2(x+4)+3x=2x+4+3x=5x+4. Find the first error and simplify correctly.

steps.title: Compare the first changed line
steps.action: The arrow from two to positive four was missed.
steps.narration: The first error appears before like terms are collected.

steps.title: Repair the bracket expansion
steps.action: Multiply two by x and by four.
steps.narration: The correct expanded form is two x plus eight plus three x.

steps.title: Collect x terms
steps.action: Two x and three x make five x; eight stays.
steps.narration: The repaired answer is five x plus eight.

worked_examples.misconception: Trusting a later line after the first incorrect arrow.
worked_examples.repair: Replay only the missing 2×4 arrow then retry.

worked_examples.q: A rectangle has length (x+4) cm and width (2x-1) cm. Write a simplified expression for its perimeter and find it at x=3.
worked_examples.answer: P=6x+6 cm; at x=3, P=24 cm.

steps.title: Trace all four sides
steps.action: Place both different dimensions into two copies each.
steps.narration: Perimeter counts two lengths and two widths.

steps.title: Combine inside the grouped sum
steps.action: One x plus two x makes three x; four minus one gives three.
steps.narration: Simplify the inner length-plus-width before doubling.

steps.title: Double the complete group
steps.action: Two times three x plus three gives six x plus six centimetres.
steps.narration: Distribute two to both parts.

steps.title: Use the given value
steps.action: At three the perimeter is eighteen plus six, or twenty four centimetres.
steps.narration: Verify with four concrete sides.

worked_examples.verify: At x=3: length 7 cm, width 5 cm; 7+5+7+5=24 cm.
worked_examples.misconception: Using area units or forgetting two sides.
worked_examples.repair: Trace each of the four boundaries before substituting.

worked_examples.q: Show that 3(x-2)+2(x+1) simplifies to 5x-4. Check at x=2.

steps.title: Expand both sides of the sum
steps.action: Three multiplies both first terms; two multiplies both second terms.
steps.narration: Distribution is an identity for every x.

steps.title: Sort like terms
steps.action: Put x terms together and signed constants together.
steps.narration: The brackets are no longer needed after their products are shown.

steps.title: Compute the general simplified form
steps.action: Five x minus four matches the claim.
steps.narration: This algebra shows equivalence for every x.

steps.title: Check one numerical case
steps.action: At x=2 both forms give six.
steps.narration: A single input illustrates rather than proves the general identity.

worked_examples.verify: For all x distribution gives 5x-4; at x=2 original 3(0)+2(3)=6 and 5(2)-4=6.
worked_examples.misconception: Treating one matching input as the proof.
worked_examples.repair: Derive the identity before substituting the check value.

steps.title: Expand the first bracket
steps.action: Two times three x is six x and two times negative four is negative eight.
steps.narration: Leave the other two groups intact for now.

steps.title: Finish the remaining paths
steps.action: Distribute minus one and divide both numerator terms by three.
steps.narration: Keep the sign switch and quotient in separate lanes.

steps.title: Sort matching term types
steps.action: Collect six x, negative x and four x; group the three signed constants.
steps.narration: An x term cannot combine with a constant.

steps.title: Add each signed group
steps.action: Six minus one plus four is nine; negative eight minus five plus two is negative eleven.
steps.narration: The result is nine x minus eleven.

worked_examples.misconception: Losing the negative bracket or dividing only one numerator term.
worked_examples.repair: Finish each operation lane before merging them.

worked_examples.skill: Simplify with a restricted variable divisor

model.description: Simplify with a restricted variable divisor

steps.title: Split and divide the numerator
steps.action: Eighteen x squared divided by six x is three x; negative twelve x over six x is negative two.
steps.narration: x cannot be zero in the original denominator.

steps.title: Distribute negative two
steps.action: Negative two times x is negative two x; negative two times negative three is plus six.
steps.narration: Both bracket terms receive the factor.

steps.title: Sort terms and constants
steps.action: Three x, negative two x and positive x form one bin; negative two and positive six form another.
steps.narration: Do not merge the two term types.

steps.title: Calculate both bins
steps.action: The variable bin gives two x and the constant bin gives four.
steps.narration: Keep the restriction from the original expression.

worked_examples.misconception: Cancelling at zero or losing the positive six.
worked_examples.repair: Mark the domain first, then make quotient and bracket paths independently.

practice_questions: Negative two times negative five is positive ten.
Divide termwise and keep the restriction.
Correct 3(x+2)+x=3x+2+x. Give the first error and correct simplified form.
A rectangle has length (x+3) cm and width (x+1) cm. Simplify P=2(l+w) and find P at x=2.
Show 2(x-3)+3(x+2) simplifies to 5x. Check at x=1.
Expand generally before testing a value.
Keep x nonzero and divide both terms.
mastery_questions: A rectangle has length (2x+1) cm and width (x+2) cm. Simplify its perimeter and find it at x=2.
P=6x+6 cm; at x=2, P=18 cm
P=2[(2x+1)+(x+2)]=2(3x+3)=6x+6 cm; x=2 gives length 5 cm, width 4 cm, perimeter 18 cm.
